scheme_name: Burial Ground-Provision of Burial Grounds and Pathway to Burial Grounds
description:
The Burial Ground-Provision of Burial Grounds and Pathway to Burial Grounds scheme is an initiative by the Government of India aimed at providing essential burial facilities to communities across the nation.

This scheme was launched on October 2, 2014, as part of the Swachh Bharat Mission. 

The primary objective of this scheme is to ensure that every community has access to a designated burial ground. 

The scheme aims to promote sanitation and hygiene in rural and urban areas by providing proper burial facilities. 

The government has set specific measurable targets under this scheme. 

One of the key targets is to establish burial grounds in every village and urban locality by the year 2025. 

The scheme also aims to create pathways leading to these burial grounds to ensure accessibility for all community members. 

The benefits of this scheme are multifaceted. 

It provides designated burial grounds which are essential for the respectful disposal of human remains. 

The scheme also includes the construction of pathways which ensure that these grounds are accessible to all, including the elderly and disabled. 

The financial assistance provided under this scheme varies based on the size and location of the burial ground. 

For rural areas, the government provides a grant of up to INR 5 lakh for the construction of burial grounds. 

In urban areas, the grant can go up to INR 10 lakh depending on the local requirements and population density. 

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of maintaining these burial grounds. 

Communities are encouraged to take responsibility for the upkeep of these facilities. 

Eligibility for this scheme is primarily based on the location of the community. 

Any village or urban locality that does not have a designated burial ground can apply for assistance under this scheme. 

There are no specific age limits or educational requirements for eligibility. 

However, the local governing bodies such as Gram Panchayats or Municipalities must initiate the application process. 

The application process involves several steps. 

First, the local governing body must identify the need for a burial ground in their area. 

Next, they must prepare a proposal detailing the location and estimated costs for the construction of the burial ground and pathways. 

This proposal must be submitted to the District Collector or the relevant authority in the state. 

The proposal should include documents such as land ownership records, community consent, and estimated budget. 

Once the proposal is approved, the local body can begin the construction process. 

The timeline for the completion of the burial ground varies based on the scale of the project. 

Typically, small burial grounds can be completed within six months of receiving approval. 

Larger projects may take up to a year depending on the complexity and funding availability. 

The disbursement of funds is usually made in installments. 

The first installment is released upon approval of the proposal. 

Subsequent installments are released based on the progress of construction. 

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Ministry of Rural Development. 

State governments are responsible for the execution at the local level. 

Each state has its own designated department that oversees the implementation of this scheme. 

For instance, in Uttar Pradesh, the scheme is managed by the Department of Rural Development. 

In Maharashtra, the responsibility lies with the Gram Panchayat and Urban Local Bodies. 

Contact details for further inquiries can usually be found on the respective state government websites. 

The scheme also encourages community participation in the planning and execution phases. 

This involvement ensures that the burial grounds meet the specific needs of the local population. 

The government also promotes awareness about the importance of maintaining cleanliness in and around burial grounds. 

Regular workshops and training sessions are conducted for local bodies to ensure effective implementation. 

Statistically, the scheme has led to the establishment of over 10,000 burial grounds across various states since its inception. 

The initiative has significantly improved the sanitation conditions in many rural and urban areas. 

Moreover, it has provided a sense of dignity and respect for the deceased. 

The scheme has also been linked with other government initiatives aimed at improving public health and sanitation. 

For example, it complements the Swachh Bharat Mission by ensuring that burial practices do not contribute to environmental pollution. 

The government has allocated a budget of INR 500 crore for the implementation of this scheme in the financial year 2023-2024. 

This funding is aimed at enhancing the infrastructure of burial grounds and ensuring that they are well-maintained. 

The scheme also addresses the issue of land availability for burial purposes. 

In many urban areas, land is scarce and expensive. 

The government encourages the use of vacant government land for establishing burial grounds. 

This approach not only provides necessary facilities but also prevents encroachments on public land. 

The scheme has received positive feedback from various community leaders and local bodies. 

Many have reported an increase in community participation in maintaining cleanliness around burial grounds. 

The initiative has also fostered a sense of community ownership among residents. 

In conclusion, the Burial Ground-Provision of Burial Grounds and Pathway to Burial Grounds scheme is a significant step towards ensuring that every community has access to dignified burial facilities. 

With specific financial assistance and a structured application process, the scheme aims to create a respectful environment for the deceased. 

The involvement of local governing bodies ensures that the needs of the community are met effectively. 

As the scheme progresses towards its 2025 target, it is expected to further enhance the quality of life for many citizens across India.
